messages.author: ca9707e227b6d438
messages.subject: Standardised Priors
parts:
Hi all,


I am running a bsem model and using priors from a very similar study.

 I was wondering when I specify specific prior for a path, should I be specifying the beta from the original study or the unstandardized coefficient. And by extension, should the precision be based on the variance of the unstandardized or standardized coefficient? 

If it is treating the prior as the unstandardized coefficient, is there a way to make blavaan use the standardized distribution as the beta?  

Thanks!

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Standardised Priors
parts:
Daniel,

blavaan models are estimated using "unstandardized" parameters, so
priors are always for unstandardized parameters. If you have an
informative prior for a standardized coefficient, maybe you could see
whether it is possible to translate this prior to an unstandardized
coefficient, based on what you know about the variance parameters in
the model. But there is not an automatic way to do this.

Ed
